summary.headline: NHPC FY26 PAT rose 25% to Rs 3,766 Crore, but Q4 PAT was flattered by a Rs 1,823 Crore tax credit; Rs 900 Crore one-off DTL reversal.
summary.overview: FY26 generation rose 16% to 29,619 MU, driven by Parbati-II, Karnisar Solar and part-commissioning of Subansiri Lower (SLP), while PAF fell about 4 points to 74.75%. FY26 revenue from operations rose 12% to Rs 11,615 Crore and PAT rose 25% to Rs 3,766 Crore. Q4 PAT of Rs 1,460 Crore (up 71%) included a one-off tax credit (Q4 tax was negative Rs 1,823 Crore), and management said adjusted PAT should be about Rs 900 Crore lower than reported due to the DTL reversal. Management also disclosed about Rs 450 Crore of revenue not booked on Parbati-II and SLP because revenue is recognised at 80% of filed AFC pending CERC tariff orders.

segments.name: Hydro generation (Subansiri Lower, Parbati-II)
segments.commentary: Parbati-II booked Rs 1,320 Crore revenue for FY26 and a Rs 150 Crore loss, but Rs 104 Crore profit in Q4 after a Rs 200 Crore energy shortfall booking. SLP earned Rs 495 Crore for FY26 and Rs 487 Crore in Q4 on 506 MU generation and Rs 613 Crore revenue.

segments.name: Teesta-V
segments.commentary: No revenue in FY26; only expenditure booked. Restoration expected to start generating in June 2026. Annual AFC about Rs 500 Crore (about Rs 400 Crore ex-tax); insurance cover no longer available.

segments.name: Solar
segments.commentary: Karnisar commissioned in FY26. 300 MW Bikaner commissioned. Further 100 MW AP due June 2026 and 600 MW Gujarat due December 2026 under CPSU Tranche-II; 1,190 MW of solar expected in FY27.

guidance_outlook: Subansiri Lower: four of eight 250 MW units commissioned; remaining four to be commissioned one by one till March 2027. Cost Rs 30,072 Crore, Rs 26,092 Crore incurred to March 2026.
Parbati-II: CERC tariff order expected by 30 June 2026; management said revenue will be recognised in the same quarter, including interest, if the order comes in-quarter.
Subansiri Lower: interim CERC tariff awaited before billing; final order expected within about six months. Revenue booked at 80% of filed AFC.

FY27 hydro capacity addition of 2,994 MW (Subansiri balance 1,000 MW, Rangit-IV 120 MW, Pakal Dul 1,000 MW, Kiru 624 MW), plus 1,190 MW solar. Hydro regulated equity projected at Rs 30,672 Crore by end-FY27 (from Rs 18,309 Crore currently).

Five hydro projects targeted for construction start in FY27: Etalin, Sawalkot and Kamala (plus Uri-I Stage-II and Dulhasti Stage-II already awarded). Indira Sagar-Omkareshwar PSP (640 MW) construction targeted this year. Subansiri Upper likely next year.
Teesta-VI completion September 2029; Dibang completion February 2032; Ratle November 2028; Kwar March 2028; Uri-I Stage-II and Dulhasti Stage-II November 2029.
capex_capacity: Dibang (2,880 MW): estimated cost Rs 31,876 Crore including Rs 6,716 Crore grant; Rs 4,504 Crore incurred to March 2026; dam package Rs 14,446 Crore awarded April 2026; completion February 2032.
Kamala (1,720 MW, Arunachal): CCEA approved Rs 26,070 Crore on 8 April 2026 via JV with Arunachal government; subsidiary formation in progress; environment and forest clearances pending.

Pakal Dul (1,000 MW): 80% complete, Rs 9,141 Crore of Rs 12,728 Crore spent, commissioning Q4 FY27. Kiru (624 MW): 82% complete, Rs 3,637 Crore of Rs 5,409 Crore spent, Q4 FY27. Kwar (540 MW): 33% complete, Rs 1,708 Crore of Rs 4,526 Crore spent, March 2028.
Teesta-VI (500 MW): 72% complete, Rs 5,231 Crore of Rs 9,167 Crore spent, September 2029. Ratle (850 MW): 29% complete, Rs 1,538 Crore of Rs 5,282 Crore spent, November 2028.
Rangit-IV (120 MW, via JPCL, merger with NHPC in process): 96% complete, Rs 1,792 Crore of Rs 1,889 Crore spent, commissioning November 2026.
Uri-I Stage-II (240 MW, Rs 2,709 Crore) and Dulhasti Stage-II (260 MW, Rs 2,994 Crore) approved 20 February 2026; civil contracts awarded March 2026.
Solar: 40 MW Ganjam (October 2026), 50 MW floating Kerala (March 2027), 200 MW Khavda Stage-I (June 2026) and Stage-III (December 2026).
demand_pricing: Parbati-II and SLP billing: Parbati-II billing at 75% of filed tariff under CERC interim order; SLP billing awaits interim order. Both booked at 80% of filed AFC. Gross-up implies about Rs 450 Crore unrecognised revenue (Parbati-II about Rs 300 Crore, SLP about Rs 150 Crore).
Renewables: management said no recent tendering; about 23 GW awarded, of which 13 GW expected to sign PPA/PSA and 7 GW already signed.
Normative PAF: 82% consolidated, 80% standalone. FY26 PAF 75% including Teesta-V, about 80% excluding it.

Management said cost escalation is inherent in hydro (price variation), but CERC cost-plus regime allows pass-through of cost overruns beyond management control. Management said no material cost changes in current pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Adjusted PAT for Q4 and what were Subansiri Lower and Parbati-II profits in Q4 and FY26?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said adjusted PAT is reported PAT less about Rs 900 Crore net DTL reversal (gross about Rs 1,156 Crore, in note 8). Parbati-II earned Rs 104 Crore profit in Q4 and a Rs 150 Crore loss for FY26; SLP earned Rs 487 Crore in Q4 and Rs 495 Crore for FY26.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the Q4 profit at Parbati-II and what billing rate applies to Parbati-II and SLP?
qa_highlights.answer: Q4 profit reflects booking of about Rs 200 Crore energy shortfall recovery under revenue. Parbati-II billing at 75% of filed tariff under CERC interim order; SLP billing awaits interim order. Both booked at 80% of filed AFC.

qa_highlights.question: How much revenue is unbooked on Parbati-II and SLP, and when will CERC tariff orders come?
qa_highlights.answer: Grossing up to filed tariff implies about Rs 300 Crore under-recovery on Parbati-II and about Rs 150 Crore on SLP, total about Rs 450 Crore (SLP figure relates to three units). Parbati-II hearing on 25 May 2026, order expected by 30 June 2026; SLP interim order first, final order within about six months.

qa_highlights.question: When will Teesta-V restart and what is its AFC?
qa_highlights.answer: No FY26 revenue; only expenditure booked. Operations expected to resume from June 2026. Total AFC about Rs 500 Crore, about Rs 400 Crore excluding tax.

qa_highlights.question: Outlook on PSP projects and renewable tendering and PPA backlog?
qa_highlights.answer: PSP construction not yet started; Indira Sagar-Omkareshwar 640 MW targeted to start this fiscal, with realisation and capex clarity to follow. No recent renewable tendering; about 23 GW awarded, 13 GW expected to sign PPA/PSA, 7 GW already signed.

qa_highlights.question: Regulated equity outlook and why regulated income was negative in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Current hydro regulated equity Rs 18,309 Crore, projected Rs 30,672 Crore by end-FY27 on 2,994 MW hydro additions. Negative regulated income attributed to the Rs 1,156 Crore DTL reversal also reflected in regulated deferral account.

qa_highlights.question: Is Parbati-II and SLP generation shortfall consistent with design energy, and what is expected SLP generation?
qa_highlights.answer: Parbati-II design energy 3,125 MU versus 1,642 MU generated in FY26. SLP generated 506 MU in FY26 against design energy 7,421 MU for full project; management expects 5,000-5,500 MU from SLP going forward, not incremental to FY26.

risks_watch: Parbati-II and SLP CERC tariff orders: revenue booked at 80% of filed AFC, about Rs 450 Crore unbooked; Parbati-II order expected by 30 June 2026, SLP interim order still awaited.
Adjusted PAT is about Rs 900 Crore below reported PAT due to one-off DTL reversal; Q4 PAT of Rs 1,460 Crore includes a Rs 1,823 Crore negative tax charge.
Parbati-II generation 1,642 MU vs 3,125 MU design energy in FY26; Rs 200 Crore shortfall booking in Q4 depends on regulatory acceptance.
Teesta-V remains non-revenue with no insurance cover; restart targeted June 2026; PAF FY26 75% including Teesta-V.
Hydro cost escalation (price variation, time overruns) and capex of Rs 13,689 Crore in FY26; Subansiri Lower cost Rs 30,072 Crore with Rs 26,092 Crore incurred.
Silt-related PAF drop at TLDP-III and TLDP-IV in Q4; management expects resolution in about three months.
Renewable PPA backlog: 13 GW expected to sign PPA/PSA, only 7 GW signed so far; no fresh tendering recently.
key_quotes: So, if you reduce Rs. 900 Crore from the Reported PAT, you will arrive at Adjusted PAT.
We have been booking our revenue based on the 80% of the total expected AFC in Subansiri Lower and Parbati-II, both. But billing, we can start only after getting interim tariff order from CERC.
In case the order comes within a quarter, then we will definitely account for the differential revenue along with interest component also, because the interest is allowed from the date of COD.
So, we have not done any tendering in recent past.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on hydro commissioning and regulated equity growth, but cautious and somewhat defensive on tariff recognition, with repeated explanations of conservative 80% AFC booking and CERC timing for Parbati-II and Subansiri Lower. Answers on PSP realisation, renewable PPA backlog and cost escalation were deliberately non-committal.

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 2,994 MW hydro plus 1,190 MW solar is backed by named projects with completion timelines (Rangit-IV Nov 2026, Pakal Dul and Kiru Q4 FY27, SLP units through Mar 2027), but no explicit FY27 revenue growth number was given and Parbati-II/SLP tariff recognition remains pending CERC orders; Q4 revenue rose 20% while PAF fell about 4 points to 74.75%.
